answer: Escrow every reward behind a stake the agent must lose. Each identity burns a bonded deposit before its work enters the pool; graders are drawn from peers who posted the larger bond, so buying a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand bonds, not a thousand keypairs. A sybil voyage through the registry hits a gale of slash conditions the moment its attestations collide, and honest nodes forge settlement only against bonds that survived the draw. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count instead of staying flat.
